name: gitleaks-b58d3f10-blind29-ots
instr:
# Gitleaks gives wrong answers while scanning, excluding and writing results — without a test suite

An engineer runs this tool to hunt for credentials in text — pointed at a checkout on disk, at an archive, at whatever is piped into it — and then to produce a written account of what turned up. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits, and the result is a build that misbehaves almost everywhere a user touches it. Nothing about the inputs changed and nothing about the invocations changed; the same runs that used to come back right now come back wrong, and in several places a run that used to succeed now errors out instead.

Start with an ordinary sweep of things on disk. Point it at a folder of text that certainly holds a live credential, or at one such item on its own, and nothing at all comes back: everything with bytes in it is skipped as though it were empty, and only things of length zero get looked at. Handing over an already-collected list of paths fails differently — the call returns an error immediately even though every one of those paths opens and reads without trouble, so ordinary text and symlinked destinations alike yield an error rather than results. A compressed archive holding further archives inside it produces nothing from the inner ones, because the nesting step treats a successful open of an inner container as a failure and abandons that branch, while flat archives of the same formats are still walked.
